summary: Shingen Takagi specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Tohoku University and Rissho University (PhD) under Gisho Nakano, Yusho Miyasaka, Ensho Kanakura, and Hakuyu Hadano. He served as assistant professor (attested 1970) and president (attested 1991–1995) at Koyasan University.

Shingo Einoo is an Indologist and religious studies scholar. He completed his PhD under Wilhelm Rau at the University of Marburg (~1980–1986). His career includes positions at the National Museum of Ethnology (~1979–1989), the University of Tokyo, and the Institute for Advanced Studies on Asia (~1989–2013).

Working in religious studies, Tibetology, and philosophy, Shinichi Nakazawa studied at the University of Tokyo (~1970–1977). He has held academic posts at Chuo University (~1993–2006), Tama Art University (~2006–2011), and Meiji University (~2011).

Shinichi Tsuda works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Akira Hirakawa and earned a PhD at the Australian National University under J.W. de Jong and A.L. Basham, later holding posts at Toyo Bunko, Eastern Institute, and ICPBS.

Shinjiro Kazama is a linguist who studied at Hokkaido University (~1984–1994). He served on the faculty at Tottori University (~1994–2006) and became a professor at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (~2006).

Shinjo Hinonishi worked in Buddhist and religious studies and studied under Shigeru Gorai. He spent his career at Koyasan University, where he served as assistant professor (attested 1980) and professor (attested 2008).

Shinjo Kawasaki is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology who studied at the University of Tokyo under Hajime Nakamura and others. He served as a Fulbright lecturer at the University at Buffalo (~1961–1963) and researcher at Toyo Bunko (~1964–1975).

Shinjo Suguro was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy who earned his doctorate from the University of Tokyo. He was vice director at the Institute for the Comprehensive Study of the Lotus Sutra (1980) and professor at Rissho University (~1970–1996).

Shinjosei Mochizuki was an archaeologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University (~1920–1924) and the University of Tokyo. He held a post at Tezukayama Gakuin University (~1966–1974).

Shinkai Sugawara was a Buddhist and religious studies scholar who studied at Waseda University (graduated 1951) and earned a doctorate from Taisho University (1991). He served as professor emeritus at Waseda University.

Shinkan Murakami specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He completed his doctoral studies and earned a doctorate at Tohoku University under scholars including Ensho Kanakura and Hakuyu Hadano, later serving as professor there (~1970–1996) and at Seiwa Gakuen College (~1996–2003).

Shinko Nakai was a scholar of Buddhist studies and history who studied at Kyoto Prefectural University (~1961–1965). He served as a professor, president, and professor emeritus at Bukkyo University (~1974–2014).

Shinkō Mochizuki studied at Bukkyo University, Taisho University, and the University of Tokyo. He held leadership posts including president at Shukyo University (1914–1928) and professor and dean at Taisho University (~1926–1942), and was elected to the Japan Academy in 1947.

Shinobu Arai Apple is a scholar in Buddhist studies. Her studies were conducted under doctoral supervisor Charles Hallisey (attested 2003), academic adviser Robert Bickner, and teacher Mark Csikszentmihalyi (2000).
Shinobu Yamaguchi is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. She received her PhD from Nagoya University in 1995 and served as a professor at Toyo University (attested 2015).

Shinsho Hanayama was a Buddhist studies scholar educated at the Fourth Higher School and the University of Tokyo (~1920–1923). He taught Buddhism at the University of Tokyo (~1934–1959) and held professorships at Toyo University (~1935–1950) and Kokugakuin University (~1949–1968).

Shintaro Kitano works in Buddhist studies and Indology, having studied under Kazunobu Matsuda (attested 2005). He served as a researcher at Taisho University (attested 2005) and as a part-time lecturer at Kyushu University (attested 2015).
Shinten Sakai specialized in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Shindo Shiraishi and held a post at Koyasan University (attested 1959).

Shinya Mano is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology. He has held positions as a part-time lecturer at Waseda University (attested 2015–2019) and as a research associate at SOAS University of London (attested 2019).

Shinya Moriyama works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He completed an MA at the University of Tokyo, studied under Eli Franco, and earned a Dr.Phil from the University of Vienna (~1999–2006). He was appointed to Shinshu University (~2009).
